speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you're experiencing fatigue, malaise, and unintentional weight loss. To help me narrow down the cause, have you noticed any night sweats or fevers recently? Also, have you been experiencing any changes in your bowel habits or appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: 71-year-old male. The patient complains of fatigue and malaise over the last few months. He also reports an unintentional weight loss of 18.1 kg over the past 6 months. He does not recall any changes in diet or exercise routines that could explain the weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that; losing nearly 20 kg in six months is significant. Given your age and these "B symptoms" (night sweats, fever, weight loss), could you tell me if you have noticed any lumps or swellings in your neck, armpits, or groin? Also, have you experienced any persistent cough or shortness of breath?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue and malaise. I also have Significant unintentional weight loss, No change in diet or exercise.

speaker: Doctor
text: That significant weight loss is concerning for a malignancy or chronic infection. Have you noticed any enlarged lymph nodes anywhere on your body, and do you have a history of smoking or previous cancers? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, and ESR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT: WBC Elevated with lymphocytosis; Hemoglobin Normal to slightly decreased; Platelets Normal to decreased. COMPREHENSIVE METABOLIC PANEL: NORMAL READINGS. ESR: NORMAL READINGS. FLOW CYTOMETRY: Presence of monoclonal B lymphocytes with a phenotype consistent with CLL/SLL. VITAL SIGNS: Temperature 36.7°C (98.0°F); Blood Pressure 126/74 mmHg; Heart Rate 87 bpm; Respiratory Rate 17 breaths/min. EXAMINATION: General - Patient appears chronically ill; Lymph Nodes - Bilateral cervical and inguinal lymphadenopathy palpable; Abdominal Examination - Evidence of splenomegaly upon palpation.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL). Based on the flow cytometry confirming monoclonal B lymphocytes and the clinical findings of significant lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly, the diagnosis is established. I recommend REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound to assess the full extent of splenomegaly, and we should proceed with staging to determine the appropriate treatment plan.
